short: An Ottoman victory over Russian forces that temporarily reversed some of Peter the Great's gains.
full:
In July 1711, a Russian army commanded by Peter the Great advanced into Moldavia during a conflict sparked by Charles XII's presence in Ottoman territory following his flight from Poltava. The Russian force was outmaneuvered and surrounded by a much larger Ottoman army at Stănilești on the Pruth River. Facing annihilation, Peter was forced to sue for peace.

The resulting Treaty of the Pruth required Russia to return the fortress of Azov to the Ottomans and dismantle several other southern fortifications. Although a humiliating setback for Peter, it allowed him to extricate his army intact and refocus his military efforts entirely on defeating Sweden in the north.
